title: The home page argues control and access, not features
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Runs in parallel with:** the rest of this epic
- **Unblocks:** the ladder story

---
Almost the entire appeal of Chatticus over a closed agent product is that you control it: it is your AWS account, your data, your network, MIT-licensed code you can read and fork and change. Feature-by-feature comparison against a big vendor is a fight we do not need to pick and would not win on volume.

But control alone reads as "more work for you." The second half of the pitch is the thing a closed product structurally cannot offer: **the people who wrote it run their own business on it, and buying the managed service puts you next to them.**

That is not a support tier. It is proximity to a team dogfooding an agent farm at the front of a fast-moving field, for fun and profit, and shipping what they learn into your deployment as they learn it. A closed product gives you a support queue. This gives you the developers.

Both halves have to be on the page, because each fixes the other weakness. Control without access is a self-hosting chore. Access without control is every other vendor.

**Done when:** the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason.
